posts.name: Gus_Smedstad
posts.cooked:
Ultimate Kismet vs. Hunted Naturalist, Requital Captain Cosmic, Chrono Ranger, Setback, and Guise in the the Carnival with the Overly Long Name.

When I saw "ultimate" I thought this was going to be tough. Particularly since the Carnival can be really brutal. Not Rook City brutal, but still bad.

It was a surprisingly easy mint for me. Mainly because I was taking out what jinxes Kismet was playing to keep her damage down, and of course I didn't touch the talisman since it's in hot potato mode. Naturalist has Crafty Assault, Chrono ranger has his grenades, Setback has "Whoops Sorry" to take out ongoings.

I pulled a lot of stupid moves, like screwing up discards with Hyperactive Senses. I often find cards which say "put multiple cards on the top / bottom of a deck" confusing because it's not clear if I'm choosing the top card or the bottom card. In this case, I reversed it, and put the cards I meant to keep on top, and the cards I meant to discard next.

Even so, it was fairly low pressure. Kismet doesn't do a lot of damage until she gets several Jinx cards out, and I was keeping her damage down anyway with Neurotoxin Dart Thrower. Guise got Guise the Barbarian / Batant Reference early, which meant a cool 15 points of damage, and Naturalist fed him extra cards to discard for that.

I actually got some use out of Uncharmed Life. At one point You Won't Believe Your Eyes was out, and Setback used that to tank a hit so only 4 targets did themselves damage, and the card self destructed. It would have been 7 targets except that Kismet was toxined and Captain Cosmic had a bracer out, and there was only 1 attraction out.

Things did get a little dicey toward the end because Kismet drew Karmic Disjunction and played 4 Jinxes at once, but she was low enough that I could take her out before it became a problem.

posts.name: QuirkyDM
posts.cooked:
Easy mint here, too. The environment had zero effect on this game. A quick hint to consider is that this environment has no targets within it.

Naturalist played Hyperactive senses early and often. Besides that, it was a simple damage fest. Captain Cosmic played and destroyed lots of constructs and took a bit of damage from them, but an Energy Bracer kept that reasonable. By the end, Kismet had time to get one Jinx out which Setback got rid of. Guise drew cards until he got the standard Blatant Reference/Guise the Barbarian combo, at which point Chrono-Ranger had already put his +1 damage bounty on Kismet. Guise didn't even have time to get through a whole round of shooty fun before Kismet was out.

posts.name: starkenburg_alexander
posts.cooked:
Mint with something like 24/6/24/18/23

I also was expecting a much worse game, but I refreshed myself on what Ultimate Kismet does. I realized all I had to do was NOT do my normal strategy of keeping the Talisman away from Kismet as much as possible and ignoring the Jinxes, and instead do the opposite. I just burned Kismet down with everything I could. I used Hyperactive Senses to keep a tab on what was coming up, and will admit I also forgot that MMFFCC doesn't have any targets for Inconcieveable Obstruction so was focused on discarding that. She hardly did anything to the heroes (beyond her old boyfriend) and only got out a singular Jinx I believe. CC only got so low because he likes to live on the edge, but was otherwise a very comfortable game.

I was actually surprised at how little use I got out of Guise this game. Usually he's one of my main shenanigans/damage dealers, but the game was over before he could get going.

~Komori

posts.name: Griff's Dad
posts.cooked:
Mint, at 11/1/5/3/16 because I was stupid.

I started the One-Shot, then got distracted and came back to it later. I'd forgotten that I'd used a different power for the Naturalist, and so he didn't have any forms activated. Then I played Crafty Assault. So... I didn't destroy two on-goings.

Then Setback had to take out Hall of Mirrors and I'd already used the Temporal Grenades I had access to, so Lady Luck stayed up. I'd beaten Kismet down to 5 hp, when she had an explosion and played both Fortune's Smiles, Unlucky Break, and both Karmic Destructions in the same turn. She healed 9 points, took out all my equipment and on-goings, and had two rounds of +5 damage to all heroes. Ouch.

Fortunately, she was down low enough that I was able to win. But man, I kicked myself hard for not checking whether I had forms activated before playing Crafty Assault.
